bull_bear.body: Debt-free balance sheet; Merger of Timken GGB approved for synergies; Dividend reduced to INR 2.5/share (vs INR 36 previous special dividend) to prioritize reinvestment in growth projects.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Raw material inflation outpacing price pass-through; Delay in PPAP approvals for new plants; Geopolitical trade tensions affecting exports; Cyclical downturn in CV/Tractor segments; Rail project execution delays.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on demand stability and long-term strategy; Cautious on near-term margins due to cost inflation; Aggressive on capacity utilization and price realization efforts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Export growth to North America is accelerating (+66% YoY) despite pending trade deals; Process industry (Steel/Cement) expected to outpace Mobile/Rail in growth rate over next 2 years due to India's industrialization shift; Bharuch plant building cost was ~50% of total capex, allowing future expansion within existing structure.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Investments in new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings have taken localization efforts to new heights, helping win more business on the back of reduced lead times and additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives
- Effective utilisation of the Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities on the back of strong and stable rail demand, leading to improved production efficiency and cost management
- Deeply entrenched in core sectors and the capital goods market through direct and indirect sales and service models
- Part of the global Timken group, with The Timken Company as ultimate holding company and access to group technology under a royalty arrangement
- Debt-free balance sheet and healthy cash reserves while continuing to make strategic investments to support future growth
- Multiple awards and recognitions during the year including CII circle competitions, Best in class Manufacturing supply chain 2025, Yellow dot award 2025, Best Organizations to work 2025, Brand of the year award 2025, and recognition at the 2025 International Metallographic contest
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict and slowing global growth — Global activity faces a major test from the outbreak of war in the Middle East, with global growth forecast to decelerate to 3.1 percent in 2026 from 3.4 percent in 2025 and a larger net impact expected on emerging markets; the Chairman also describes an environment marked by geopolitical uncertainties, evolving trade dynamics and changing industrial supply chains
- Oil-import-driven terms-of-trade shock in India — India meets more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements through imports with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, so the conflict poses the risk of a significant terms-of-trade shock that could increase input costs, exert downward pressure on the rupee, and complicate inflation-growth trade-offs
- Input cost inflation outpacing pricing — Profit before tax as a percentage of revenue from operations declined compared with the previous year mainly due to increased cost of material consumed, increased depreciation charges and reduction in other income, with net material cost rising modestly faster than revenue growth
- Execution and ramp-up drag from the new Bharuch plant — Bringing a new site online requires patience and perseverance; as Bharuch ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, and higher depreciation from the new manufacturing plant added to other expenses
- Cyclicality and policy dependence of end markets — Demand is tied to government capex and industry cycles — Indian Railways budgetary support, steel and cement capacity expansion, thermal PowerGen commissioning, mining output targets and infrastructure-led commercial vehicle demand — so any slowdown in public capex directly affects the bearing demand base
- Pull-forward of tractor demand ahead of TREM V norms — The record FY 2026 tractor upcycle was partly driven by pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026, which can borrow volumes from the following year even as the CV cycle is expected to moderate to efficiency-driven growth in FY 27
- Related-party / group concentration — The Company runs material arm's length transactions with group entities — The Timken Company (Ultimate Holding Company, including royalty), The Timken Corporation and Timken Wuxi Bearings Co. Ltd. (fellow subsidiaries) — for purchases and sales of goods, making sourcing, offtake and technology access dependent on the parent group and requiring recurring Board and shareholder approvals
- Export dependence and trade-barrier exposure — Revenue growth for the year was primarily driven by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations while domestic revenue showed modest growth, leaving the Company exposed to higher trade barriers and reconfiguration of trade flows and supply chains

business.body: The Company manufactures bearings and bearing components in India, having added new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings and taking its localization efforts to new heights, which helped it take on more business through reduced lead times and additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. It is investing at its Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material to strengthen its position in the plain bearing market, and its Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities serve the rail market. The Company is well connected to the core sectors and capital goods market and is deeply entrenched through its direct and indirect sales and service models, and during the year advanced further in the Process OEMs and Distribution segment.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expand the manufacturing footprint in India and build world-class manufacturing capabilities closer to customers, of which the inauguration of the Bharuch facility was described as a defining milestone
- Broaden the product portfolio and improve responsiveness and manufacturing flexibility through the Bharuch facility, viewed through a long-term lens while initial operating and capability-building costs are incurred during ramp-up
- Deepen localization: investments in new capacity across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings, taking localization efforts to new heights and adding credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives
- Strengthen position in the plain bearing market through investments at the Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material
- Capitalise on favourable Rail market conditions to drive effective utilisation of the Jamshedpur manufacturing facilities, improving production efficiency and cost management
- Grow the Process OEMs and Distribution segment, staying deeply entrenched in core sectors and the capital goods market through direct and indirect sales and service models
- Invest decisively for growth while preserving financial strength — maintaining a debt-free balance sheet and healthy liquidity position alongside capital expenditure
- Maintain focus on operational excellence, financial discipline, and a culture of safety, quality and continuous improvement
- Continue CSR focus on education, skill development, healthcare and community development, with emphasis on underserved and vulnerable sections including the elderly, orphaned children, people with intellectual disabilities and differently abled individuals
- The Company follows a balanced approach of investing decisively for growth while preserving financial strength, maintaining a debt-free balance sheet and a healthy liquidity position even while funding new manufacturing capacity, acquisitions and a renewable-power group-captive investment. Dividend is governed by a Dividend Distribution Policy that was revised during the year, with additional factors and parameters added for determining dividend payouts which is expected to give more clarity in determining payouts; the Board recommends dividend for member approval at the AGM. The Board did not propose to transfer any amount to reserves during the financial year under review.
- Acquired approximately 26% equity in Sunstreamgreen Energy C&I Three Private Limited to secure electricity from renewable sources under the Group Captive Scheme
- Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report published, with an assurance statement from TÜV SÜD South Asia Pvt Ltd, an independent third party assurance provider, giving reasonable assurance about BRSR Core
- Internal Committee constituted at all locations of the Company under the POSH Act with at least half of the total members being women; two sexual harassment complaints were received and both were disposed of during FY 2025-26, with no case pending for more than 90 days
- Full compliance confirmed with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, with policies and procedures implemented so that all eligible women employees are granted mandated maternity benefits
- Corporate governance philosophy anchored on the core value of ethics and integrity, operationalised through the Code of Conduct / Standards of Business Ethics Policy for the Board and Senior Management, plus a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy
- Enterprise-wide Risk Management Framework for systematic identification, assessment, monitoring and mitigation of key business risks, reviewed periodically through management oversight, internal audits and Audit Committee supervision
- Particulars relating to Conservation of Energy and Technology Absorption disclosed as Annexure VI to the Board's Report
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company invested in new capacity addition across spherical roller bearings and cylindrical roller bearings, taking its localization efforts to new heights; the new capacities helped take on more business on the back of reduced lead times and with additional credentials to qualify under Make in India initiatives. The defining milestone of the year was the inauguration of the Bharuch manufacturing facility, which the Chairman describes as reflecting confidence in India's long-term industrial growth and a commitment to building world-class manufacturing capabilities closer to customers, enhancing the ability to serve customers with a broader product portfolio, improved responsiveness and greater manufacturing flexibility. Bringing the new site online requires patience and perseverance, and as the Bharuch facility ramps up the Company continues to incur initial operating costs and fund capability building, which it views through a long-term lens. The Bharuch new plant was capitalized during the year, and the Company continues with its expansion through investment in the Jamshedpur Rail project. During FY 2025-26 the Company allocated approximately 8% of its revenue for capital expenditures while maintaining a debt-free balance sheet and a healthy liquidity position, and it also acquired shares of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited and invested in the equity of a power producer company for procurement of electricity from renewable sources.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's bearing market has been growing at a CAGR of over 9.4 percent and was valued at around USD 2.9 billion in FY 2026, driven by rising demand across automotive (CVs, tractors), railways, industrial machinery and renewable energy, and boosted by localization policies, electric-vehicle trends and infrastructure development
- In FY 2027 India's bearing market is expected to see steady, structurally driven growth, supported by continued core industry, railway and infrastructure capex, stable demand from commercial vehicles and tractors, and a resilient aftermarket that cushions volume volatility
- Rail market has shown strong demand and stability, supporting effective utilisation of the Jamshedpur facilities
- Indian Railways capital allocation of about 2.62 lakh crore in FY 2026 including 2.52 lakh crore budgetary support, with record coach output exceeding 9,900 coaches and 1,914 locomotive units in FY 26, reflecting continued priority on rail infrastructure and modernization
- Steel: crude steel output up 10.7% YoY to approximately 168.4 million tonnes in FY 26; steelmaking capacity of approximately 220 million tonnes in FY 2025-26 projected to reach 300 million tonnes by 2030, with public sector capex rising nearly 44%
- PowerGen: neutral sector outlook for FY 27 with long-term electricity demand growth of 5.5-6.0 percent YoY, thermal plant utilisation projected around 65 percent over FY 26-FY 27, around 5 GW of thermal capacity expected to be commissioned in FY 27 and about 39,545 MW under construction
- Wind: India added 6.34 GW of new onshore wind capacity in 2025, the highest annual addition since 2017 and an 85% increase over the previous year; global new wind installations estimated at 178 GW in 2026 with a 5.2% CAGR forecast for 2026-2030
- Cement: grinding capacity additions of 160-170 million tonnes estimated during fiscals 2026 to 2028 with incremental demand of approximately 30-40 million tonnes per annum
- Mining: raw coal production of 1.04 billion tonnes in FY 2026 with a target of 1.31 billion tonnes for FY 2026-27; iron ore production up 7% to a record 310 million tonnes
- Commercial vehicles: FY 2025-26 volumes crossed 1 million units on capex-led, infrastructure-anchored demand, creating a stable base for moderated, efficiency-driven growth in FY 27
- Tractors: FY 2026 was a breakout year with retail sales exceeding 10.5 lakh units, driven by rural tailwinds and pre-buying ahead of TREM V norms effective April 2026
- Capital goods sector supported by sustained government infrastructure spending and emphasis on manufacturing growth, reducing import dependence and strengthening supply chain resilience
- Structural drivers of India's infrastructure, manufacturing, railways and energy transition investments, combined with increasing localisation and supply-chain diversification, create significant opportunities for industrial companies with strong technology, manufacturing capabilities and customer relationships
- Highest-ever revenue in FY 2025-26 was driven primarily by strong export sales with volume growth across geographical locations, while domestic revenue showed modest growth
- Margin headwind from initial operating costs and capability-building funding as the Bharuch facility ramps up
- Macro risk from rising oil prices and geopolitical tension, given India imports more than 85 percent of its crude oil requirements with approximately half transiting the Strait of Hormuz, posing a terms-of-trade shock risk that could increase input costs and pressure the rupee
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Timken India crossed INR 1,000 crore quarterly revenue for the first time in Q4FY26, driven by robust exports and CV demand, though margins faced pressure from rising input costs with only 10% price pass-through achieved so far. The strategic merger with Timken GGB and progressive ramp-up of the Bharuch plant (targeting 70% utilization by July) position the company for long-term synergy, despite near-term margin volatility as cost hikes are negotiated.

open.item: The Board of Directors, subject to approval of Members at the ensuing AGM, has recommended a dividend of Rs 2.5 per equity share of Rs 10 each fully paid up for the financial year ended 31 March 2026.

The Company is investing approximately Rs 38 crores to set up a manufacturing line for plain bearings at Bharuch, to be sold under the brand name GGB, with commercial production expected to start during Q2 of FY 2026-27.

The Company is investing approximately Rs 120 crores to enhance capacity of bearing components (cup and cone) at the rail facility in Jamshedpur, expected to be completed in Q3 2026-27, with project work going on as per timelines.
The Board has approved a draft Scheme of Amalgamation involving amalgamation of Timken GGB Technology Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, with the Company.
The Bharuch manufacturing facility, inaugurated during the year and capitalized in FY 2025-26, continues to ramp up with the Company incurring initial operating costs and funding capability building.
The Company is making investments at the Bharuch facility to produce plain bearings using Fiber reinforced composite (FRC) material to strengthen its position in the plain bearing market.
The Company continues with its expansion with investment in the Jamshedpur Rail project.

meta.thesis: Timken India crossed INR 1,000 crore quarterly revenue for the first time in Q4FY26, driven by robust exports and CV demand, though margins faced pressure from rising input costs with only 10% price pass-through achieved so far. The strategic merger with Timken GGB and progressive ramp-up of the Bharuch plant (targeting 70% utilization by July) position the company for long-term synergy, despite near-term margin volatility as cost hikes are negotiated.
